title: What Founders Get Wrong About Scaling – With Carta’s CEO

reader_summary.headline: I remember my first pitch and it was so bad.
reader_summary.overview: I remember my first pitch and it was so bad. The biggest difference is it's the first time in your career you worked for somebody that knows less than you do about what you do. That was Henry Ward, co-founder and CEO of Carter, a company that started reinventing the cap table way back in 2012.

key_points.text: So in today's wide-ranging conversation with A16C games partner Josh Lue, they discuss went to higher missionaries versus mercenaries.
key_points.evidence_quote: So in today's wide-ranging conversation with A16C games partner Josh Lue, they discuss went to higher missionaries versus mercenaries.

thesis: The episode discusses the distinction between hiring 'missionaries' who are deeply committed to the company's purpose versus 'mercenaries' who are hired primarily for their specific skills. It argues that while early-stage companies should prioritize missionaries to build a strong culture, the ratio of these two types of employees must shift as the company scales.
